The next thing we have to do is something about the {{Color MM3D|Red|torchlights}} in this room...|Goron|MM3D}} are recurring [[Item]]s and [[Object]]s in {{TLoZ Series}}. ==Location and Uses== Braziers are often found within [[Cave]]s or [[Dungeon]]s. They have a variety of uses from illuminating the surrounding area to being a key aspect in solving a puzzle or unlocking a hidden secret. Because of their nature of being lit or unlit, Dungeons and other areas can be designed with the prospect of [[Link]] having to take advantage of this-lighting them to cause an event or sequence like unlocking a door or revealing a [[Treasure Chest]]. Outside of being decorative, Torches are primarily used in puzzles. They can be lit by using a [[Fire]] source such as a burning [[Deku Stick]], a [[Fire Arrow]], the [[Fire Rod]], [[Din's Fire]], or the [[Lamp]]. Sometimes they can only be lit by pressing a [[switch]] or clearing a room of [[Enemy|Enemies]]. In dark areas, [[Link]] can light a Torch to light up the room. Some Braziers known as [[Face Lamp]]s can appear as traps shooting [[Fireball]]s at Link, similar to [[Medusa]]s. They are usually invulnerable to any form of attack. Additionally, In {{PH}}, some of them can be deactivated by hitting a nearby switch, or defeating all the enemies in the room. Braziers vary across the series from housing a simple group of sticks tied together as well as more elaborately designed metal ones. {{TP}} has the most variety of Torch designs in the series, with various wooden Torches, stone Torches, and other, more ancient-themed Torches. ==={{ALttP|-}}=== {{Stub|ALttP}} ==={{LA|-}}=== {{Stub|LA}} Stationary Lamps can be found in [[Dungeon]]s, [[House]]s and other inside locations. [[Link]] can light unlit Lamps temporarily by sprinkling [[Magic Powder]] on them to illuminate dark rooms or solve puzzles. Some Lamps can shoot [[Fireball]]s at Link. ==={{OoT|-}}=== {{Stub|OoT3D}} ==={{MM|-}}=== {{Stub|MM3D}} ==={{OoS|-}}=== {{Stub|OoS}} ==={{OoA|-}}=== {{Stub|OoA}} ==={{FS|-}}=== {{Stub|FS}} ==={{TWW|-}}=== {{Stub|TWW}} ==={{TMC|-}}=== Torches serve as simple decorative [[Object]]s, sources of light, [[Switch]]es, and [[Enemy|Enemies]] in {{TMC}}. Some (such as four in [[Deepwood Shrine]] and the four hidden in [[Tree]]s in [[North Hyrule Field]]) are directly connected to [[Floor Switch|Step Switches]], which, when stepped on, illuminate the Torches and produce some kind of effect. Others (such as those in the [[Fortress of Winds]], the [[Temple of Droplets]], and the [[Palace of Winds]]) shoot balls of energy at [[Link]], damaging him. These attacks can be blocked with the [[Small Shield]]. ==={{TP|-}}=== {{Stub|TPHD}} ==={{PH|-}}=== {{Stub|PH}} ==={{ST|-}}=== {{Stub|ST}} ==={{SS|-}}=== {{Stub|SS}} ==={{ALBW|-}}=== {{Stub|ALBW}} ==={{BotW|-}}=== {{Compendium/Extract|Torch}} Torches are a common [[Item]] that [[Link]] can use to carry Fire with him and spread that Fire to stationary Torches and other flammable objects such as grass, bushes, and wood. Torches can also be used as a [[Weapon]], but they have a very low attack power of 2. After being ignited by contact with a Fire, Torches stay lit until Link puts the Torch away or it rains. Torches are useful for navigating dark areas, such as the [[Thyphlo Ruins]]. Being made of wood, they will not attract [[Lightning]] during a [[Thunderstorm]], and they do not conduct [[Electricity]]. They will float in [[Water]] if dropped. After first exiting the [[Shrine of Resurrection]] and meeting the [[Old Man]] on the [[Great Plateau]], Link can steal the Old Man's Torch. He will then ask Link what he intends to use it for.{{Cite|Well then, just help yourself to that torch there. And how, may I ask, are you planning to use it?|Old Man|BotW}} If Link replies saying that he plans to use it as a Weapon, the Old Man will advise him to take his [[Woodcutter's Axe]] instead.{{Cite|[As a weapon!] Innovative... However, that is probably best used to light fires. If you need a weapon, you can find something better. Many beasts roam the land past this point. You can take my axe with you, if you please. Assuming you can find it.|Old Man|BotW}} If Link tells him that he plans to use it to light Fires, the Old Man will tell him to be cautious.{{Cite|[To set things on fire!] That is rather...unnerving. Please be cautious with that around any dry grass that might catch fire.|Old Man|BotW}} If Link refuses to tell the Old Man what he plans to do with the Torch, he will tell him to do as he pleases and will let him be.{{Cite|[It's a secret...] I see, Well then, do as you please.|Old Man|BotW}} Link can find Torches in the [[Lost Woods]], which can aid him in navigating the area by lighting Torches and watching the direction the Fire blows with the wind. Torches are also useful for lighting all of the [[Blue Flame Pedestal]]s around the [[Hateno Ancient Tech Lab]] and the [[Akkala Ancient Tech Lab]] with [[Blue Flame]], as Link must travel long distances without the Fire burning out. When placed next to a flammable [[Object]] such as [[Decorative Shrub]]s, their flames will transfer and catch the nearby Object on fire. Braziers can be learned and copied as [[Echo]]es, and have an [[Echo]] cost of two. ==Other Appearances== ==={{HW|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|HWDE}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{CoH|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|CoH}} Torches allow [[Cadence]], [[Link]], [[Yves]], or [[Zelda]] to see in the dark, light up braziers, and burn stumps that may be blocking their path.{{Cite|Increases visibility in dark areas. Can burn stumps and light up braziers.|Inventory|CoH}} However, they have a limited use and go out over time, forcing the heroes to switch between different kinds of torches in order to light their way through caves and dungeons. They can be found in red [[Treasure Chest]]s, dropped by slain enemies, or bought from a [[Shopkeeper]] for 10 [[Rupee]]s. After a [[Game Over]], Torches can also be found at the [[Fate]]'s shop selling for 1 [[Diamond]]. {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} {{Stub|AoC}} {{Noncanon|End}} ==={{AoI|-}}=== {{Stub|AoI}} ==Nomenclature== {{Nomenclature}} ==Gallery== File:TMC Torchlight Sprite 2.png|{{Game Label|{{TMC|-}}}}A stationary Brazier in Dark Hyrule Castle File:Torch2 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:Torch3 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:Torch4 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:Torch5 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:Torch6 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:Torch7 TP.png|{{Game Label|{{TP|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:TPHD Lakebed Temple Wall Torch Model.png|{{Game Label|{{TPHD|-}}}}A wall Brazier File:SS Unlit Torches.png|{{Game Label|{{SS|-}}}}Unlit stationary Braziers File:SS Lit Torches.png|{{Game Label|{{SS|-}}}}Lit stationary Braziers File:ALBW Torches.png|{{Game Label|{{ALBW|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:BotW Candlestick Model.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}A Candlestick File:EoW Brazier Model 2.png|{{Game Label|{{EoW|-}}}}A wall-mounted Brazier File:EoW Brazier Model 3.png|{{Game Label|{{EoW|-}}}}An immovable Brazier fixed to the ground File:HW Torch Model.png|{{Game Label|{{HW|-}}}}A stationary Brazier File:CoH Torch Sprite.png|{{Game Label|{{CoH|-}}}}A Torch File:CoH Brazier Sprite.png|{{Game Label|{{CoH|-}}}}An unlit Brazier File:CoH Brazier Lit Sprite.png|{{Game Label|{{CoH|-}}}}A lit Brazier File:CoH Brazier Sprite 2.png|{{Game Label|{{CoH|-}}}}A destroyed Brazier found in ??? ==See Also== {{See Also| * Battle Torch * Daily Use Goods * Glass Torch * Magic Torch * Obsidian Torch * Torch of Reflection * Torch of Wisdom }} {{Ref}} {{Categories |Daily Use Goods, One-Handed Weapons, Torches, Weapons |items= AoC |objects= LA, LADX, LANS, TMC, TP, TPHD, ST, SS, SSHD, ALBW, EoW, HW, HWL, HWDE, CoH, AoC, AoI }}
